clue.text: Theoretically, it makes us universally central

definitions.text: Theoretically, it makes us universally central

blocks.note: the surface reads it as 'in principle'; the setter means 'according to a theory', a model of the heavens
'us' is our planet, and 'universally central' means literally at the centre of the universe

explanation.walkthrough: 'Us' is the Earth: the Ptolemaic system was the ancient theory that put the Earth at the centre of the universe, so 'theoretically' and 'universally' are both literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ptolemaic system is the geocentric model of the cosmos, a theory making our planet the centre of everything.

clue.text: Maligned dove I can keep up in the air?

indicators.note: something up in the air is unsettled, so the letters have not landed in order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they can keep a dove aloft while it flutters in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird is a red herring: a dove is a pacifist, and 'maligned' tells you the answer is the sneering word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Peacenik is a dismissive, somewhat derogatory term for a peace campaigner, that is, a maligned dove.

clue.text: See 13
Creature that's drained of water's, er, done for

indicators.note: 'done for' means wrecked, so the words are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A hesitant speaker says some creature, drained of water, is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drained' reads as emptied of water, but the definition means a creature that lives in the drains; the 'er' is not filler but part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by habitat: 'drained' is bent into 'living in the drains', the brown rat's classic home.

clue.text: See 26
Jury briber supporters dividing capital return

indicators.note: the supporters split the capital in two by sitting in its middle
the capital comes back, so it is written in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: A corrupt fixer's backers split the capital before he comes home.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is rare: in law, embracery is the crime of trying to corrupt a jury, and an embrasor is the one who does it.
explanation.definitionFit: An embrasor is someone guilty of embracery, the offence of bribing or improperly influencing a jury.

clue.text: He wrote back to addressee, finally

indicators.note: only the end of 'addressee' is taken

blocks.note: the stern is the back of a boat

explanation.surface: A correspondent writes back to the person who wrote to him, at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrote back' looks like replying to a letter, but 'He wrote' is the definition, a writer, and 'back' is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was the 18th-century novelist who wrote Tristram Shandy.

clue.text: It makes Cyclops, cryptically, about the ultimate in crossword's unsubtle humour

indicators.note: the words are written in code, their letters scrambled
the ultimate letter is the last one of 'crossword'

explanation.surface: A crude crossword joke, apparently, turns someone into a one-eyed giant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It makes Cyclops' reads as a poke in the eye, the stock gag of slapstick, but it is simply the letters to scramble; 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapstick comedy is broad physical humour, custard pies and pratfalls, about as unsubtle as humour gets.

clue.text: No subject gets trim in steel tempered by sun

definitions.note: a noun phrase for an adjective: themeless means having no subject

indicators.note: the trim sits inside the steel
tempered steel has been reworked, so its letters are reshaped

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for sun (Sunday)
a hem is the trim on a garment

explanation.surface: A metalworker's recipe: trim, steel hardened by sunlight, and no subject to speak of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tempered by sun' looks like one process, but the sun is only S joining the steel before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something themeless has no subject or unifying theme.

clue.text: Spot large roomy place

blocks.note: L = large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone spots a large, spacious place to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roomy' is the joke: not spacious but full of rooms to let.
explanation.definitionFit: A motel is a place full of rooms for travellers.

clue.text: Rock ’n' roll classic clue stuffed with wicked content

indicators.note: the clue's letters are rolled around, doing double duty with the definition
the clue is filled with the wicked word
content is what is held inside, so the wicked word sits within the clue

explanation.surface: A famous rock 'n' roll song is described as a crossword clue packed with naughty material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll' does double duty, belonging to the definition and also telling you to roll CLUE around.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucille is Little Richard's 1957 rock 'n' roll hit.

clue.text: Superior aid distribution or rapid transport

indicators.note: the letters are carried off to new places

explanation.surface: Comparing better ways to deliver aid: distribution or quick transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superior' means from above, not better: the aid arrives from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: An airdrop distributes supplies by dropping them from aircraft, from above.

clue.text: Fish-eater's brother close up

blocks.note: a brother in a religious order

explanation.surface: A fish-eater's brother shutting up shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'has'; the answer runs on into 3 down.
explanation.definitionFit: The monk seal is a seal species, and seals live on fish.

clue.text: Glowing with colour, one possibly cycles a bit

blocks.note: cycling is one way of riding, hence 'possibly'
a cent is a small coin, a bit of money

explanation.surface: Someone flushed and glowing after a short bike ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' flags an example: cycling is one kind of riding.
explanation.definitionFit: Iridescent means shimmering with changing rainbow colours.

clue.text: Which might reveal one's inner thoughts of careless penmanship?

definitions.text: Which might reveal one's inner thoughts of careless penmanship?

blocks.clueFragment: Which might reveal one's inner thoughts
blocks.note: a psychological assessment, the Rorschach, in which a patient describes what they see in a shape
read literally, an examination of sloppy handwriting, whose tell-tale sign is a smudge left by the pen

explanation.walkthrough: Read one way it is a psychological test; read another it is a test of sloppy handwriting, since an inkblot is what careless penmanship leaves behind. The answer runs on into 25 down.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkblot (Rorschach) test uses blots of ink to reveal a person's inner thoughts.

clue.text: No more fencing for camp men about to retire?

definitions.note: cryptic: the final post of a fence, after which the fencing stops
the bugle call for soldiers going to bed, not the soldiers themselves

blocks.note: the final post of a fence, where the fencing ends
the bugle call sounded as soldiers turn in for the night

explanation.surface: A rule at a camp: no more fencing practice for the men about to retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retire' means go to bed, not stop working: the Last Post is the military bugle call sounded at the end of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: The final post ends a run of fencing, and the Last Post is the call played for soldiers turning in.

clue.text: China capped electric leads on memory microchip

indicators.note: the leading letters of 'capped electric' are taken

blocks.note: first letters of capped and electric
an integrated circuit, the formal name for a chip

explanation.surface: A tech report: China puts a cap on electric cables running to a memory chip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country in a tech story, but it is porcelain; 'capped' and 'electric' only supply their first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: China is fine porcelain, a kind of ceramic.

clue.text: MASH director, who wants paying

indicators.note: to mash is to crush into a new shape

explanation.surface: The director of the film M*A*S*H is waiting for his fee.
explanation.walkthrough: MASH looks like the title of Robert Altman's film, but it is an instruction to mash up DIRECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A creditor is someone owed money, who wants paying.

clue.text: Man flu, old style, you could say, post operations here

indicators.note: the man and the flu are to be spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: rheum is an old word for a cold or catarrh

explanation.surface: Someone describes a case of man flu in old-fashioned terms, then goes for surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post operations' looks like after surgery, which suits the flu story, but post means letters and parcels.
explanation.definitionFit: A mailroom is where an organisation's post is handled.

clue.text: Not a straightforward critic of unrestricted, wide press coverage of Independent

indicators.note: the letters are freed from their order
the scrambled press covers the Independent

explanation.surface: A media critic complains about unregulated, sweeping press coverage of The Independent, the British newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all about journalism, but 'press' is only anagram fodder with 'wide'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideswiper takes indirect digs, a critic who never attacks head-on.

clue.text: Doctor Sorrows is boring

definitions.note: a verb phrase: drills means bores

explanation.surface: A dull doctor's personal troubles: his woes are tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' means tedious on the surface but making holes in the definition, as a dentist's drill does.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who drills is boring holes.

clue.text: "Charge" contained by concise reference work?

explanation.surface: A lexicographer's question: is the word 'charge' included in the shorter dictionary?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contained by' looks like an instruction to put something inside, but it simply gives IN; 'concise' tells you the reference work is abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the legal sense: bringing a formal accusation of a crime against someone.

clue.text: See 23
Record down in the charts? That can be a real pain

definitions.text: That can be a real pain

blocks.note: a record losing places in the charts has fallen back

explanation.surface: A singer groans that their record is falling in the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces read in reverse order of the clue; the answer runs on into 22 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipped disc in the spine is notoriously painful.

clue.text: Provisional playwright drops leading character: one is contracted

indicators.note: the playwright loses his first letter

explanation.surface: A provisional playwright drops a lead character because he is under contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading character' sounds like the star of a play, but it is PINTER's first letter; 'one is' becomes I AM, contracted.
explanation.definitionFit: Interim means provisional, in place for the time being.

clue.text: See 15
Lives in Lille's changed together with a former immigration HQ

indicators.note: 'lives' goes inside the changed letters
LILLES has its letters changed around

explanation.surface: Life in Lille has changed, as has a former immigration headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lives' is a verb giving IS (to be is to live), not the noun; the answer runs on into 5 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellis Island in New York harbour was the main US immigration station until 1954.

clue.text: Darn leisure activity?

definitions.note: an interjection standing for a mild oath, which is a cross word

blocks.note: a mild oath, the kind of angry exclamation said when annoyed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Darn' looks like mending socks, a leisure activity itself, but it is a mild curse: a cross word.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword is a puzzle done for pleasure, and a cross word is an angry one like 'darn'.
